entry.title: TTB: Test-time Baking for Efficient Rendering of Decoder-only View Synthesis Models
entry.summary:
Decoder-only Large View Synthesis Models (LVSMs) with KV-cache have recently achieved state-of-the-art quality by regressing novel views from neural networks without reconstructing 3D geometry, while Test-Time Training (TTT) layers save computation but sacrifice quality. We propose Test-Time Baking (TTB), a strategy that learns to bake global scene information from cross-view attention into a lightweight MLP, enabling fast and high-fidelity novel-view decoding. The first key is to repurpose the fast-weight MLP of TTT to learn the cross-view attention mapping explicitly from its input-output pairs, rather than replacing attention entirely, achieving the same rendering efficiency as TTT while delivering substantially higher quality.

Source: Hugging Face Daily Papers · Tags: #llm #open-weights #neuroscience

entry.title: Open Vision Banana: A Fully Open Recipe for Generative Visual Perception. Recent work suggests that pretrained image generators encode real-world understanding beyond image synthesis.
entry.summary:
Recent work suggests that pretrained image generators encode real-world understanding beyond image synthesis. Vision Banana exploits this by framing vision tasks as conditional image editing. However, its data, weights, code, and implementation details are not public.

entry.title: Actor, Judge, or Teacher? Understanding Decision Models in Long-Horizon Agents
entry.summary:
Decision models answer a question with a typed output, such as a choice among options with a probability for each, so one model can choose an agent's actions, evaluate actions already taken, or score every action to teach a policy with reinforcement learning. Prior work has studied them mainly as actors, judging their usefulness by how well they act. We ask whether a decision model that acts poorly can still teach well.

entry.title: Ropedia Xperience 2: A Gold Standard for Scaling Physical AI Environments and Behaviors
entry.summary:
Large foundation models such as GPT-6 Astra and Claude Fable 5.1 have recently been shown to control robots directly from visual observations. They nevertheless remain brittle on long-horizon, contact-rich tasks in real-world environments. Further progress depends on two complementary resources: demonstrations of human behavior that supervise how tasks are performed, and interactive environments in which policies can be rolled out, evaluated, and improved in closed loop.

entry.title: Unbundling Multimodal Vision Encoding. How multimodal language models should encode visual input remains up for debate.
entry.summary:
How multimodal language models should encode visual input remains up for debate. Most models use a pretrained vision encoder, while some recent recipes train the encoder from scratch with the language model or remove it entirely. Vision encoders bundle together three design choices: a visual prior from upstream pretraining, dedicated vision capacity, and pre-fusion placement of that capacity (i.e., before the multimodal backbone).

entry.title: Factored One-sided Adam-Moment for Practical and Scalable SOAP
entry.summary:
Second-order optimizers (e.g., Shampoo, SOAP) have emerged as compelling alternatives to Adam/AdamW and promise faster per-step convergence than AdamW in transformer training. However, they still remain costly in practice, and even SOAP still pays substantial optimizer-state memory and eigendecomposition overhead. We ask whether the benefits of SOAP can be retained at nearly the efficiency of AdamW.

entry.title: Back to Pixels: Lifting Latent Video Diffusion into Pixel Space. Frontier video generation models work in a VAE latent space that compresses video in both space and time.
entry.summary:
Frontier video generation models work in a VAE latent space that compresses video in both space and time. This compression made training tractable, but now limits high-resolution, controllable, and interactive generation -- doubling resolution quadruples token count, conditions apply to groups of frames rather than individual ones, and each response must wait for the rest of its multi-frame block. We present PixVid, a simple yet effective method that lifts a pretrained latent video model to directly generate every frame in pixel space.

Source: Hugging Face Daily Papers · Tags: #llm #open-weights #clean-tech #computer-vision

entry.title: TurtLES: A Large-Scale Benchmark for Turbulent 3D Neural PDE Surrogates
entry.summary:
Machine-learning surrogates are increasingly used to accelerate computational fluid dynamics, yet progress is limited by the lack of benchmarks capturing realistic, time-dependent turbulent flows. We introduce TurtLES, a 14 TB dataset of 3D turbulent cylinder wakes in the shear-layer transition regime, computed via high-fidelity implicit large-eddy simulations. The dataset contains 400 trajectories of 400 time steps each, with 3-11 million points per frame, spanning variations in geometry, Reynolds number, and angle of attack.

Source: Hugging Face Daily Papers · Tags: #llm #open-weights #analysis-pde #neuroscience

entry.title: JustRUA: A Controlled Study of GPT-6 Robot-Use Agents
entry.summary:
GPT-6 Astra can drive a robot arm directly through a fixed harness, and scores of such robot-use agents on RoboDojo have risen quickly since. Reported systems differ in harness and test subset and often change several designs at once, so it is hard to tell which choices produce the gains. We take these designs apart and test them in one framework, along the harness around the model, the action interface, the reuse of experience and the scene geometry given to the model.

Source: Hugging Face Daily Papers · Tags: #llm #open-weights #agents #robotics
